why: A (universes at 0) states Lemma 11.3.2 under weaker hypotheses, as the item's title says. Well-definedness, functoriality of F_*Θ and F^*F_*Θ = Θ need only fullness of F; F_*F^*Θ' = Θ' needs only essential surjectivity; invariance of F_* under natural equivalence needs fullness of F and G, and invariance of F^* needs nothing. Θ is any functor to ℚ, of any sign. A also adds (G∘F)^* = F^*G^*, (G∘F)_* = G_*F_* (full functors), 1_* = id and three groupoid facts (eq_of_isomorphic, isomorphic_obj, isomorphic_of_full). B states the text's lemma for an equivalence and functors to ℚ⁺. A_to_B takes each claim of B from the matching conjunct of A, since an equivalence is full and essentially surjective. It uses the non-item IsEquivalence.exists_iso for the existence of x, and the V11_14 lemma pushforwardTheta_nonneg for 0 ≤ F_*Θ. B_to_A is vacuous: A's generality and its extra conjuncts are not consequences of B. It re-proves all fifteen statements outright, with local copies of the project's proofs. B_to_A_on_domain (rt_check OK) shows that B does give A's central claim on its own domain: (F_*Θ)(y) = Θ(x) for every F(x) ≅ y, from F^*F_*Θ = Θ and the functoriality of F_*Θ. On the text's statement the two sides agree; A is a generalization.
